cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is still speaking to the people, laying out how they're to live. Now he's talking about keeping things fair. Every town, for every tribe, gets judges and officials.

cards.question: Judges and officials in every town. How does Moses say they're to judge the people?

cards.text: Then Moses says: don't deny justice, don't show partiality and don't accept a bribe. No favorites, friend, not even for the guy who tells me my hat looks GREAT.

cards.question: Moses says a bribe even gets to the wise and the righteous. What does it do to them?

answers.text: Blinds their eyes and twists their words
Makes them rich and then makes them lazy
Turns their whole town against them

cards.question: Moses says to pursue justice, and justice alone, so that you may live and possess the ___ the LORD your God is giving you.

cards.text: Then Moses turns to worship. Don't set up a wooden Asherah pole next to the altar you will build for the LORD your God.

cards.question: Moses names one more thing Israel must not set up for themselves, something the LORD hates. What is it?
Next up, sacrifices. True or false: Moses says an ox or a sheep with any defect or serious flaw must not be sacrificed to the LORD.

cards.text: A flawed one is detestable to the LORD, Moses says. That's like me handing a baker the cookie I dropped on the floor and calling it a GIFT.
Now a serious case. What if a man or woman in one of Israel's towns is found breaking the LORD's covenant and worshiping other gods, even bowing down to the sun or moon?

cards.question: Somebody reports that a person in town is worshiping other gods. What does Moses say to do first?

answers.text: Send them out of the land

cards.text: If the report is true, Moses says that person is to be brought out to the town gates and stoned to death.

cards.question: Moses says a death sentence like this can't rest on just anyone's word. How many witnesses does he require?

cards.text: The hands of the witnesses go first in putting him to death, and after that, the hands of all the people. Moses says you must purge the evil from among you.
Some cases will be too difficult to judge in town, like bloodshed, lawsuits or assaults.

cards.question: When a case is too difficult to judge in town, where does Moses say to take it?

answers.text: The place the LORD will choose

cards.question: At the place the LORD will choose, Moses says to go to the Levitical ___ and to the judge who presides at that time.

cards.text: They inquire, and those leaders give a verdict in the case. So does that verdict leave any wiggle room?

cards.question: True or false: Moses says people can adjust the verdict a little if they disagree with it.

cards.text: Moses says to abide by their verdict and do everything they instruct: "Do not turn aside to the right or to the left from the decision they declare to you." You know when you drift one street off and the GPS on your phone shouts RECALCULATING?

cards.question: What does Moses say must happen to a man who acts presumptuously and refuses to listen to the priest or the judge?

answers.text: He must be put to death
He pays a fine to the priests
He is sent out of the town

cards.question: True or false: Moses says when all the people hear that the man who refused the priest or the judge was put to death, they'll be afraid and stop behaving arrogantly.

cards.text: Now Moses looks ahead to when Israel is settled in the land and the people say they want a king like all the nations around them. You know when everybody in the group chat gets the new phone, and suddenly you NEED one too?

cards.question: If Israel sets a king over itself, who does Moses say chooses him?
True or false: Moses says Israel may set a foreigner over them as king as long as he's a strong leader.

cards.text: Then Moses gets to the king himself, starting with horses. He's not to get many horses or send the people back to Egypt for more.

cards.question: Why can't the king send the people back to Egypt for horses?

answers.text: The LORD said never go back that way
Pharaoh won't sell horses to Israel
The road there is far too dangerous

cards.question: Moses says the king must not take many wives for himself, or his ___ could go astray.
True or false: Moses says the king may pile up large amounts of silver and gold for himself.

cards.text: Here's my favorite part. Once he's seated on his royal throne, the king must write for himself a copy of this instruction on a scroll, with the Levitical priests right there.

cards.question: The king's scroll stays with him. How long is he supposed to keep reading from it?

answers.text: All the days of his life

cards.question: Reading it and carefully keeping it helps the king learn to ___ the LORD his God.
True or false: Moses says keeping the instruction on his scroll means the king's heart won't be exalted above his countrymen.
What does Moses say comes to a king who keeps this instruction?

answers.text: He and his sons reign many years
He never loses a single battle

cards.text: And he won't turn aside to the right or to the left. That line again, friend, and Moses isn't done preaching yet.
